one_month_reasoning: Window to 2026-11-19 holds: Q3 2026 results and the 2027-2031 capital/financing plan on Oct 29 before the open [11] (management said on the Q2 call [6] the 5-year update comes with Q3); the Nov 3 midterms (MN and CO statewide races matter for regulation and CO wildfire legislation); the MN gas decision and CO gas / NM electric settlements in Q4 [2]; and the 10y, which is 5.12% on 2026-10-20 after peaking at 5.31% on Oct 5 (4.75% at end-July) [19] and explains most of the slide since Q2. The plan roll-forward should lift rate-base growth (prior $60B base + $10B+ line of sight [3]), but incremental capex comes with ~40% equity [3], and the NSPM 2027-28 base-rate freeze filing [20] and the PSCo historical-test-year order [21] give the call a lag topic, so I see no directional edge; Q3 consensus $1.37 [15] is near guidance pace. Anthropic's IPO: Bloomberg reports formal marketing as soon as the week of Nov 9 and trading before Thanksgiving (Nov 26) [22], so pricing likely lands at or just after the window's end. A large raise can pull money from AI-beta and 'AI power' names, but XEL's holders are mostly yield/defensive, so I add only a small extra left tail (3% weight on a ~$72 component), no tilt. Centre ~$76.8, monthly sigma ~5.8% (19%/3.5 = 5.4% plus an earnings/plan-day bump).

XEL TTM EV/EBITDA ~14.9x (EV $85.3B = 624.6M x $76.68 + $37.4B net debt, over F92 $5,720M) sits above the 4-peer NTM median 10.25x because XEL's EBITDA lags its 17% rate-base step-up in 2027; not used as a leg.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: Discount held at today's level, not closed: (1) wildfire liability is un-legislated in Colorado (management calls it a 2027 priority [6]) and live in Texas (AG suit for damages and civil penalties [7]; ~$80M of the $525M Smokehouse policy left [2]); (2) the plan needs $7B of equity (85% contracted [3]) plus ~40% equity on incremental capex; (3) lag is getting worse, not better, in the near term: PSCo earns ~7.2% vs 9.3% allowed [3] and its new rates use a 13-month historical test year [21], and NSPM proposes a 2027-28 base-rate freeze [20]. Against that, EPS growth (~8.6% in my build, +10.2% consensus FY27/FY26 [15]) beats the 7.8% peer median, so I do not widen it toward ES. The discount narrows only on CO legislation (bull).

thesis_break_reason: $61 is ~12.8x my NTM EPS ($4.77) and ~13.7x today's NTM consensus, at or below the cheapest peer (ES 13.7x) and below the $64.7 zero-growth capitalised value; it is ~11% under the $68.72 52-week low, which XEL made with the 10y at its 5.31% peak in early October [19]. A rates-only bear (10y 5.5-6%, P/E -2 turns to 15.2x) gives a P/E leg of ~$69.5; the engine's blended bear ($59.8) is pulled down by the DCF leg's rate sensitivity, not by how utilities trade. So a close below $61 most likely means a fundamental break: a new at-fault wildfire with liability beyond insurance, a Texas AG outcome that blocks recovery, a regulatory reset (ROE cuts, MN plan rejected with a punitive case, disallowed data-center capex) or a downgrade that forces block equity. I keep $61 rather than $63: $63 sits about one 12-month sigma below spot at 19% vol, within ordinary rate-driven range.

Size of equity in the new 2027-2031 plan (Oct 29): incremental capex is funded ~40% with equity, so a bigger plan raises EPS growth less than rate base.
Regulatory lag: PSCo earns ~7.2% vs 9.3% allowed and its new rates use a historical test year [21]; NSPM's proposed 2027-28 base-rate freeze [20] depends on how much the ITC acceleration offsets.

Conversion of the >20 GW data-center pipeline into signed ESAs (~2 GW contracted plus Google pending), the MPUC's ruling on the Google ESA under MN AG opposition [23], and who bears stranded-cost risk.
Wildfire: Texas AG civil-penalty suit; a new at-fault fire in CO or the TX Panhandle before liability legislation passes.

No verified Anthropic load in Xcel territory: the Abernathy (SPS) campus is a Fluidstack project with a Google backstop [8], TeraWulf sold its stake to a Fluidstack-led group, and Anthropic's named TeraWulf lease is in Hawesville, Kentucky [14].

long_dated_risks.cash_flow_effect: Base plan has very little data-center load [6], so the hit is to the $10B+ incremental capex: 2028-30 EPS ~2-3% lower and a ~0.5-turn lower multiple. Counterparty loss falls first on the large-load tariffs (MN: 15-year minimum term, minimum bills, exit fees, credit requirements; CO proposal: 80% minimum bill, six-month deposit, exit fee [12]); at Abernathy power is 100% passed through to the tenant with a Google backstop [8]. Six months of deposit is small against 15-year generation, so a neocloud default would push disputed costs into rate cases (regulatory risk to shareholders) rather than straight to earnings. Anthropic's S-1 (WSJ: ~$450B cloud commitments, Google $111B, >$160B TPU lease [18]) strengthens Google, Xcel's largest data-center counterparty, which lowers this risk at the margin.

reverse_dcf_check: The 17.2x horizon P/E leg ($81.92) is reproduced by the engine DCF at a WACC of ~5.6% (vs 5.94% CAPM) with 3.5% terminal growth, i.e. it implies regulated returns capitalised at ~1.3x rate base EV and rate base growth of ~11-13% through 2030 then ~3.5%. That is plausible only if (a) the capex plan is executed with constructive orders (recent orders at 9.2-9.6% ROE [3,21] support it, though on historical test years in CO), and (b) the 10y does not settle above ~5.5%; the post-horizon risks above (wildfire, higher-for-longer rates, backlash, data-center slowdown; net about -$4.6/sh probability-weighted before the CO-legislation upside (+$1.9)) are why the multiple stays at today's 9% discount rather than at the peer median.

(3) Valuation: 17.2x (today's 0.91x relative to the 18.85x peer median [17], held because its causes persist) on NTM EPS $4.77 = $81.92; driver DCF $55.31 at 5.94% WACC (10y 5.12% [19]) with horizon net debt rebuilt from a cash-flow bridge ($50.1B, vs $44.1B straight-lined in round 1, because 2026-27 capex is front-loaded [3]); blend $76.6 at the 0.2 DCF weight, i.e. fairly priced. (4) WSJ/Anthropic [18]: ~$450B of cloud commitments (Google $111B, AWS $110B, >$160B Google TPU lease) and 'could spend $750B' are a general positive for data-center demand, mostly through Google, which is Xcel's largest data-center counterparty (Pine Island ESA [7], Abernathy backstop [8]). I dropped round 1's tracker label on Abernathy: TeraWulf's filing names Fluidstack as tenant with a Google backstop [8], TeraWulf sold its stake to a Fluidstack-led group, and Anthropic's named TeraWulf lease is in Kentucky [14], so I found no verified Anthropic load in Xcel territory. The S-1's warning about organised data-center opposition matches what is visible in MN (AG vs the Google ESA [23]) and CO. Counterparty risk sits first with the large-load tariffs' minimum bills, deposits and exit fees [12], and disputed amounts would go to rate cases. (5) On Kilian's IPO-liquidity question: Bloomberg has marketing from the week of Nov 9 and trading before Thanksgiving [22]. XEL's holders are yield/defensive and its base plan carries little data-center load [6], so a drain should hit AI-beta and 'AI power' names more. A flow-driven dip to ~$70 with the 10y stable and the Oct-29 plan intact would be a buying opportunity (~9% under fair value $76.6, plus a 3.1% yield [10]); a drop driven by the 10y above ~5.5%, a punitive MN outcome or a new wildfire is not. Thesis break $61. (6) Ladder: the engine mixture (bear $59.8 p0.25 / base $76.6 p0.55 / bull $90.4 p0.20, 13% within-scenario vol) is left-skewed because the DCF leg is very rate-sensitive in the bear, so I blend it 50/50 with a lognormal at the fair value and 18% vol (realized 19%), with 3% weight on a wildfire/regulatory crash tail near $55. Median ~$75.5. Price-only: the ~$2.40 of dividends paid before the horizon is excluded.

discount_rate.basis: CAPM cost of equity 7.37% = 10y UST 5.12% (Treasury par curve, 2026-10-20) + beta 0.5 x ERP 4.5%; pre-tax marginal debt cost 5.2% (2026 OpCo/HoldCo issues at 4.85-5.875%) x (1-21%) = 4.11%; market weights E 56.1% (624.6M sh x $76.68 = $47.9B) / D 43.9% (net debt $37.4B, F91): 0.561 x 7.37% + 0.439 x 4.11% = 5.94%. Engine EBIT is entered after tax (NOPAT incl. AFUDC), so tax_rate 0 and the debt shield sits in the WACC.

model_inputs.structure_note: Regulated utility: value carried by a P/E leg (weight 0.8) on a rate-base EPS build (avg rate base x 53.5% equity ratio x earned ROE ~8.2-8.7% less HoldCo drag, divided by the forward-equity share path), plus a driver DCF (weight 0.2 per the forward-P/E band 15.0-19.6x; XEL at 16.9x FY2027 consensus). Engine 'EBIT' = NOPAT incl. AFUDC (ongoing net income + after-tax interest) so the engine's NOPAT reproduces the EPS build; revenue is total operating revenue (fuel is pass-through, so margins are not economic margins). Capex is the $60B base plan by year plus $10B line-of-sight phased 2027-30; FY2030 capex is normalised to D&A + 3.5% x ~$103B rate base so the Gordon terminal starts from steady state (growth capex after 2029 assumed to earn about its cost of capital). Shares and net debt at the horizon are stated directly because the engine's bridge has no equity issuance. EV/EBITDA is not used as an engine leg because engine EBITDA is NOPAT-based; it is a narrative cross-check only. METHOD-FIT flag (no XBRL revenue/market cap) is a tagging artifact: revenue $14,669M comes from the Q4 2025 release and market cap from F89 x price, so it does not weaken the methods; the zero-growth capitalised-earnings leg is the added non-multiple check.
model_inputs.gap_note: fair_value.value equals the engine base horizon value.
model_inputs.dcf_check: DCF $55.31 is ~32% below the P/E leg ($81.92). The gap is the discount rate plus the front-loaded capex: the P/E leg implies a WACC of ~5.6% (engine reverse DCF) vs 5.94% CAPM, the DCF's terminal is ~109% of EV because 2026-29 FCFF is deeply negative (capex 60-100% of revenue), and every 25bp of WACC moves the DCF ~$14-17/sh ($72.7 at 5.69%, $41.1 at 6.19%). Rebuilding horizon net debt from a cash-flow bridge ($50.1B vs $44.1B straight-line) cost the DCF ~$9/sh (6,000/662), which is why the gap widened from 23% in round 1. Regulated utilities trade at ~1.3x rate base EV because allowed ROEs (9.3-9.6% [21,3]) exceed the ~7.4% CAPM cost of equity, value a CAPM DCF with a 3.5% terminal capitalises poorly. I keep the playbook weight (0.2, forward P/E 16.9x) rather than tuning the WACC: it pulls the blend ~$5 below the P/E leg, a deliberate rates-risk haircut.
